claims.statement: The product CLI is the console script powercontext, which maps to powercontext.cli.app:main; the separate powercontext-ops script maps to powercontext.ops.__main__:main.
The powercontext.cli entry-point group registers the code, config, doctor, observability, service, server, setup and archive command providers.
create_cli builds the root from content command groups first, then from entry-point providers sorted by name, and rejects a provider whose command name is already registered.

Optional command providers for the builtin and server roles are skipped, not failed, when the role's declared requirements are not installed at compatible versions; requirement checks follow powercontext extras recursively.
A provider whose module is missing raises a RuntimeError asking for repair, and a provider that does not load a Typer application raises a TypeError.

Root options --server-url, --allow-insecure-http, --timeout and --json are stored lazily in the Click context by configure_client; no Client is constructed until a content command runs, and root overrides take precedence over environment and saved settings.
Content command groups registered by the client CLI include live, ready, capabilities, stats, import-sessions, dream, topic-memory, candidate, experience, skill, external-skill and scope.

ClientSettings reads the POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_ prefix: POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_SERVER_URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000, POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_API_TOKEN defaults to unset as a secret, POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_TIMEOUT defaults to 10.0 seconds and must be greater than zero, and POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP defaults to false.

When no explicit URL is passed, the shared policy resolves the endpoint from POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_BASE_URL or POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_SERVER_URL, then the saved endpoint for the host in clients.json, then the default http://127.0.0.1:8000.

Plaintext consent is resolved from the explicit argument, then host-specific and common environment variables, then saved consent only when the saved endpoint equals the resolved endpoint, otherwise false.
Saved HTTP consent is bound to its endpoint: an invocation-level URL override does not inherit saved consent for a different endpoint.

The shared Client configuration is a version 1 JSON file at POWERCONTEXT_CLIENT_CONFIG_FILE or ~/.config/powercontext/clients.json, storing non-secret per-host server_url, allow_insecure_http and target fields; setup persists only these fields and publishes credentials separately.
The shared network policy treats only http URLs with non-loopback hosts as plaintext non-loopback; loopback is 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and localhost, and classification performs no DNS lookup or request.

PowerContextClient refuses to send any request over non-loopback plaintext HTTP unless allow_insecure_http is set, and a caller-supplied http_client is trusted only when trust_transport_security is also true.
The facade's own httpx client bypasses environment and OS proxies for loopback targets only; remote targets keep normal proxy behavior, and aclose closes only a client the facade created.

Every facade request sends the X-PowerContext-Dream-Contract header with value 2, adds a Bearer Authorization header only when a token is configured, and injects tracing headers; the response request ID is carried into errors.

Facade request failures are classified: an httpx error becomes a TransportError, an undeclared status becomes a ServerResponseError built from the Server error body, and a success body that fails validation becomes an InvalidResponseError.
PREPARE_CONTEXT omits assembly when unset and omits include_receipt and include_reuse when false, so that a newer client does not send fields an older Server would reject.

Host native transport resolution returns an endpoint and consent flag as a read-only diagnostic, and it raises a fixed error for unsupported, unreadable or $include-based native configuration rather than guessing an endpoint.
For Codex, the endpoint comes from the installed Codex plugin's MCP URL when the plugin cache and plugin exist; otherwise resolution falls back to the saved endpoint or the default.

Host endpoint precedence differs by host: claude-code and hermes use host-specific environment, then native configuration, then common URL, then saved endpoint; zcode and kimi-code fall back to the default rather than the saved endpoint; openclaw raises when no endpoint is configured; other hosts use host environment, common URL, native configuration, then saved endpoint.
Native transport resolution fails rather than choosing one endpoint when ZCode Hook and MCP URLs differ or when WorkBuddy Hook and MCP URLs differ.

Native consent overrides the shared consent only when no host environment consent variable is set; the result is false when the native value is false, and true only when the native URL equals the chosen endpoint (Claude Code and Hermes always apply the override); OpenClaw and DSH require the native consent value to be a boolean.
Doctor resolves each installed host's endpoint through the native resolver and records a failed transport diagnostic when that resolution raises, without hiding completed installation checks.

Setup chooses the endpoint in order: explicit --server-url with conflicting environment overrides rejected; otherwise a single agreeing value from the setup environment file or process environment; otherwise saved or native candidates; otherwise POWERCONTEXT_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL, the declared TCP listener port, or the default; a UDS-only listener is rejected for agent setup.

Setup refuses a remote plaintext endpoint before any installation side effect unless consent is explicit, offering an interactive prompt only on a TTY outside JSON mode with default no; accepted remote HTTP still prints a warning that TLS verification and Server authentication are unchanged.

import-sessions supports only the codex host, scans CODEX_HOME sessions JSONL files, and extracts only user message prompts while excluding host-generated synthetic messages and prompts without a working directory.

Session import resolves each prompt's Scope through session and workspace binding keys with allow_default disabled, skips the prompt as unresolved_scope on a 404 or 422, and never falls back to the default Scope unless an explicit scope ID is given.

Session import redacts known environment and Codex auth secrets before capture, skips prompts that are empty after redaction or longer than 200000 characters, and gives each captured prompt a deterministic Source ID derived from scope, session, turn and the original unredacted content so reruns address the same Source.

Session import checkpoints record accepted, redaction-conflict and failed outcomes atomically; a checkpoint with another schema or destination is ignored, accepted items are skipped on rerun, and failed items are retried.
Session import dry-run performs discovery, redaction and scope checks without capturing Sources or writing the checkpoint, and reports no checkpoint file in its summary.
Client-facing CLI commands exit with code 1 on a ClientError and session import exits with code 2 on a SessionImportError.

Root options --server-url, --allow-insecure-http and --timeout default to unset and --json defaults to false; unset values defer to environment variables, saved settings and ClientSettings defaults (127.0.0.1:8000, consent false, 10.0 seconds).
The source-management registration adds the source and credentials command groups to the same product CLI root.
Content commands with --json write the operation's full response model as JSON; without --json they print a human summary through the response renderer.

When import-sessions runs with an explicit scope and the Server is unreachable, each prompt is recorded as failed with capture_failed and the run still exits 0; without an explicit scope, the transport error during scope resolution aborts the run with exit 1.

With an explicit --scope-id, import-sessions skips per-prompt Scope resolution and captures every discovered prompt into that Scope; without it, scope-resolution errors other than 404 or 422 propagate and abort the import.
import-sessions leaves --dry-run off by default and stores its checkpoint at CODEX_HOME/.powercontext/session-import/codex.json unless --checkpoint-file names another path.
Setup treats only non-loopback http endpoints as remote plaintext, so loopback HTTP needs no consent, and setup rejects a UDS-only listener because it has no TCP endpoint for an agent.

Setup consent takes an explicit flag first, defers to process environment consent overrides, then uses the setup environment file and DSH native consent before the shared resolver applies saved consent that matches the endpoint.

Undeclared 401, 403 and 503 responses map to UnauthorizedResponseError, ForbiddenResponseError and UnavailableResponseError, which are subclasses of ServerResponseError; other undeclared statuses map to ServerResponseError.
